rv.q: But, although David Eldridge's riveting new play has its roots in this allegiance-shifting Essex town, he also uses it to explore the rancour, grudge-bearing and obsession with property among migrant East End families. The result is the best play about British working-class life since Peter Gill's The York Realist .
It’s all beautifully controlled in Dominic Cooke ’s brilliantly cast production...
